judgment.rationale: First SFI is Grade 1 / Term 3 / Reading and Phonics / Group Guided Reading: 'Reads aloud from own book in a guided reading group with teacher, that is, the whole group reads the same story'. Second SFI is Grade 1 / Term 1 / Listening and Speaking (Oral) / Twice weekly focussed listening and speaking activities: 'Participates in discussions, taking turns to speak and respecting others in the group'. Both are Grade 1 (rank 1) and both are enacted in a teacher-led small-group oral setting, so co-operative group behaviour (turn-taking, respecting others) meaningfully complements and reinforces taking one's turn to read aloud in a guided reading group. However, the substantive capability targeted differs: the Term 1 statement targets discussion participation and social listening/speaking conduct, while the Term 3 statement targets oral reading of connected text from own book, whose core demands (decoding, word recognition, fluency) are not supported by the discussion statement. The nomination evidence is only a shared Grade ancestor, same-grade local rank, and token/trigram overlap on generic words ('group', 'in', 'the'), which is not developmental evidence. Hence complementary coherence without a justified developmental dependency: relatesTo rather than buildsTowards in either direction. Note that both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and one LC bundle is truncated, so some pair-specific detail may be unavailable; the available text is nonetheless unambiguous about each statement's focus.

judgment.rationale: First SFI: Grade R (rank 0, resolved), Term 3, Skill Area EMERGENT WRITING, Sub-strand 'Emergent Writing' - 'Draws pictures to convey a message about a personal experience and uses this as a starting point for writing. With help adds a word or phrase to a drawing'. Second SFI: Grade 1 (rank 1, resolved), Term 1, Skill Area WRITING, Sub-strand 'Shared, Group and Independent Writing' - 'Draws pictures to convey a message. For example, about a personal experience'. They share Learning Component 27cea6a6-0a5a-5cb9-b7f0-414320ed128a ('Draws pictures to convey a message about a personal experience'), whose claims cite both SFIs, so the coherence is at the level of the same instructional capability rather than incidental wording. This is meaningful reinforcement: the same drawing-to-convey-a-personal-message skill recurs as learners move from the emergent-writing strand into the formal Writing strand, giving useful pair-specific instructional coherence. It is not a justified developmental step: the Grade 1 statement is no more demanding than the Grade R statement and is in fact narrower, since the Grade R text already requires using the drawing as a starting point for writing and adding a word or phrase with help. The only signal of increased independence is the sub-strand heading, which is hierarchy evidence and cannot by itself license buildsTowards under the configured requirement of substantive extension. Symmetric relatesTo with null direction therefore applies, retaining canonical endpoint order. Evidence limitations: 24 omitted source-evidence items for each endpoint, truncated supporting LC evidence for both, and upstream audit/merge context on both endpoints and all supplied ancestors; these warnings are retained and the judgment rests on the supplied statement text, coordinates and shared LC rather than the complete source record.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade 3, Term 4 Skill bullets under the same WRITING / 'Shared, Group and Independent Writing' sub-strand, printed in the same table row and page (index 132). 'Writes a selection of short texts for different purposes such as recounts, dialogues' is a composition skill, while 'Uses apostrophes in contractions such as can't, Mary's' is a specific punctuation convention (LC tags: apostrophes, contractions, punctuation, writing). They cohere substantively as complementary composing and written-convention skills applied in the same independent writing work, but the evidence shows no developmental dependency: apostrophe use is a narrow convention not required for producing recounts/dialogues, and composing short texts does not presuppose contraction punctuation. Same canonical rank (Grade 3) and same Term 4 provide no basis for a directional claim, and the shared tokens ('as', 'such', 'writing') are generic. Symmetric relatesTo is therefore the supported judgment; both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each), which limits but does not contradict this reading.

They are coherent, complementary oral-language skills taught in the same term: attentive, non-interrupting listening behaviour accompanies the comprehension/retelling work of sequencing story events (shared LC tag 'listening'). The evidence does not, however, show one as a substantive developmental extension of the other — one is a listening-etiquette/turn-taking behaviour and the other a story-comprehension recall skill — and same-rank, same-term placement alone is insufficient to assert a directional buildsTowards. Remaining token/trigram and page-proximity signals are weak and generic, so a symmetric relatesTo best fits the bounded evidence; note that source evidence for both endpoints and LC evidence for the second endpoint are truncated.

judgment.rationale: Both SFIs are Grade R, Term 1, Listening and Speaking (Oral), under the same 'Daily activities' sub-strand (coordinate rank 0 for both, same page). 'Listens to short stories with enjoyment and joins in choruses at the appropriate time' and 'Sings simple songs and does actions (with help)' are complementary oral-participation skills: joining in choruses and singing simple songs with actions both involve attentive listening and timed group vocal participation, giving genuine conceptual coherence beyond shared parent or generic token overlap (shared tokens are only 'the', 'to', 'with', 'and'). However, neither statement is evidenced as more complex or as supporting success in the other: they are parallel same-term bullets with no expanded capability (both scaffolded, 'with help'/'appropriate time'), and within one grade a later-to-earlier direction is not at issue since both sit in Term 1. Developmental dependency is therefore unsupported, so the symmetric relation is used. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated, but the full statement text and Learning Components supplied are sufficient for this judgment.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade R (rank 0) Emergent Writing / Handwriting readiness Skills: the first is Term 1 'Develops eye-hand co-ordination: plays catch with bean bags, balls... draws with crayons or paints informally during outdoor play', the second is Term 2 'Develops fine motor skills for strengthening hand muscles: rolls plasticine, models with play dough... threads lacing cards, beads'. They share the Grade R ancestor and the handwriting sub-strand focus, and their LCs share the tags 'handwriting'/'emergent'. However, they address distinct, parallel physical-readiness components (visual-motor co-ordination versus hand-muscle strength/dexterity) through different play activities; the Term 2 statement is not an expansion or deepening of the Term 1 statement, and proficiency in catching/informal drawing is not evidenced as support for plasticine/threading hand-strengthening. This is substantive complementary coherence within handwriting readiness rather than a developmental dependency, so relatesTo rather than a Term 1 to Term 2 buildsTowards. Evidence is limited: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and both carry upstream audit/merge context.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade 1 Skills (rank 1) sharing only the Grade banner ancestor: the first is Term 1 WRITING / Shared, Group and Independent Writing ('Writes a caption for a drawing or picture'); the second is Term 2 LISTENING AND SPEAKING (ORAL) / Twice weekly focussed listening and speaking activities ('Listens to stories with interest, drawing a picture to show understanding'). The overlap flagged by nomination is the token/trigram 'drawing/picture' and the LC tag 'drawing', i.e. drawing as a shared representational response mode, not a dependency: the second statement's substantive demand is sustained listening to stories and showing comprehension (LCs 'Listens to stories with interest', 'Draws pictures to show understanding of a story'), whereas the first demands written caption production. Caption writing does not materially support listening comprehension, and the later-term listening skill does not require caption writing, so no developmental direction is warranted despite the admissible Term 1 to Term 2 ordering; the coherent link is complementary use of drawing/picture alongside emergent writing. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), but the full statement texts, terms, skill areas and LCs are present and consistent.

judgment.rationale: Both SFIs are the verbatim CAPS bullet 'Uses handwriting tools effectively: pencil, eraser, ruler' (identical description hash, identical LC e4680267 with identical tags), located in the same Writing / Handwriting sub-strand: the first under Grade 2 (rank 2) / Term 4 and the second under Grade 3 (rank 3) / Term 1. The nomination signals are purely similarity-based (token, trigram, tag and LC jaccard 1.0) plus weak local rank proximity, which cannot by themselves establish developmental dependency. No substantive extension is visible in the endpoint statements: the same three tools and the same 'effectively' criterion recur unchanged, and the bounded surrounding context does not show increased demand (Grade 2 Term 4: children 'continue to use print script ... but begin to learn a type of joine[d]' script; Grade 3 Term 1: children 'may still be using print script in written recording until the end of the second te[rm]'). Accordingly buildsTowards is not warranted. The recurrence is nonetheless instructionally meaningful rather than generic: the identical handwriting tool-control skill is deliberately carried across the Grade 2 to Grade 3 boundary within the same Writing/Handwriting sub-strand, giving pair-specific coherence and reinforcement without dependency, so the symmetric relatesTo decision (null direction, canonical endpoint order preserved) is appropriate. Confidence is moderated because both endpoints' source evidence (24 omitted items each) and LC metadata are truncated and all endpoint/ancestor nodes carry upstream audit/merge context.

The second SFI (Term 1) is recognition of common vowel digraphs ('oo' as in moon, 'ee' as in tree); the first SFI (Term 2) applies vowel digraphs together with consonant blends to build 3-, 4- and 5-letter words. This is substantive extension from aural/visual recognition of a digraph unit to productive multi-letter word building combining additional phonic elements, so proficiency in the earlier Term 1 recognition skill supports success in the later Term 2 word-building skill. Direction runs from the earlier Term 1 node (second) to the later Term 2 node (first), consistent with within-grade term ordering. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each) and both carry upstream audit/merge context, but the retained statement text and identity scopes are sufficient and non-contradictory.
